'''''Dittrichia graveolens''''', commonly known as '''stinkwort'''<ref name=k/> or '''stinking fleabane''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> is a plant species in the [[Asteraceae|sunflower family]], native to southern Europe,<ref>[https://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/floraspecie.php?genere=Dittrichia Altervista Flora Italiana genere Dittrichia] includes photos and European distribution maps</ref> North Africa, and western Asia as far east as Pakistan. It has become naturalized in California, Asia, Africa, Australia, and other places and is regarded as a [[noxious weed]] in some regions.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Dittrichia%20graveolens.png|title=Biota of North America Program, 2014 county distribution map|website=Bonap.net|access-date=19 March 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://bie.ala.org.au/species/urn:lsid:biodiversity.org.au:apni.taxon:614530|title=Atlas of Living Australia, ''Dittrichia graveolens'' (L.) Greuter, Stinkwort|website=Bie.ala.org.au|access-date=19 March 2022}}</ref><ref name=GRIN>{{GRIN|name=''Dittrichia graveolens'' (L.) Greuter|id=401641|access-date=2014-06-16}}</ref><ref name="UC Davis">{{cite journal|last=Brownsey|first=Rachel |author2=Guy B. Kyser |author3=Joseph M. DiTomaso|date=April–June 2013|title=Stinkwort is rapidly expanding its range in California|journal=California Agriculture|publisher=University of California|volume=67|issue=2|pages=110–115 |doi=10.3733/ca.v067n02p110 |url=http://wric.ucdavis.edu/PDFs/CalAg6702p110-2013.pdf|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Ortiz |first=Edward |url=http://www.sacbee.com/2013/08/12/5642385/stinkworts-fast-growth-could-threaten.html |title=Stinkwort's fast growth could threaten California's wine growers - Agriculture - The Sacramento Bee |website=Sacbee.com |date=2010-07-28 |access-date=2013-08-14 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130814141929/http://www.sacbee.com/2013/08/12/5642385/stinkworts-fast-growth-could-threaten.html |archive-date=2013-08-14 }}</ref> It is a classified as an [[invasive species]] in California, and a potential threat to [[California wine|wine production in the state]].<ref>''Weeds of California and Other Western States, Volume 1'', Joseph M. DiTomaso, Evelyn A. Healy. UCANR Publications, 2007. page 350</ref>

The plant is a branching [[subshrub]] growing up to {{Convert|130|cm|abbr=off}} tall, with an aromatic, [[camphor]] smell.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fisheries |first=Agriculture and |date=2015-10-30 |title=Stinkwort |url=https://www.business.qld.gov.au/industries/farms-fishing-forestry/agriculture/biosecurity/plants/invasive/other/stinkwort |access-date=2023-07-12 |website=www.business.qld.gov.au |language=en-AU}}</ref> Leaves are long and narrow, pointed at each end, with small [[Leaf shape|teeth]] along the edges, [[Gland (botany)|glandular]] hairs on the surfaces, and a sticky resin. One plant can produce numerous yellow [[flower heads]] with as many as 16 [[ray florets]] and 40 [[disc floret]]s.<ref name=k>{{Cite web|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=250066482|title=Dittrichia graveolens in Flora of North America |website=Efloras.org|access-date=19 March 2022}}</ref>

Barbs on the fluffy-tipped seeds, which help it spread, can fatally damage the digestive systems of grazing animals. Oils in the plant also taint the flavor of meat and milk of animals that have consumed them. The sticky resin has been known to cause allergic reactions and severe [[dermatitis]] in humans.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aphis.usda.gov/sites/default/files/Dittrichia_graveolens_WRA.pdf|format=PDF|title=Weed Risk Assessment for Dittrichia graveolens (L.) Greuter (Asteraceae) : Stinkwort|website=Aphis.usda.gov|access-date=19 March 2022}}</ref> For this reasons, it is advisable to wear protective gloves when handling the plant.
